name: Risograph Printing
visualIdentity: Explicit printmaking direction: two ink colors on natural paper, with overprints creating additional tones. Controlled grain, dots, and slight registration offsets give a tactile printed feel. Registration errors remain stable rather than jittering.
suitableUses: Suitable for posters, illustrations, zine-like social posts, editorial title cards, event promos, explainers and illustrated product stories. Chapter transitions or scroll-led storytelling can help when the narrative has meaningful stages. These are inferred fits from the stated visual and motion guidance.
limitations: Keep text readable and the palette to two independent inks; overprint is the only added tone. Avoid small coral text, gradients, extra inks, smooth vector shadows, per-frame grain reseeding and morphs that break plate alignment. Omit chapter motion when boundaries obscure causality, interrupt a continuous shot or loop, or add no narrative value.
palette: Use natural paper with exactly two inks. Optional suggested tokens: paper #F4EBD8, blue #254687 and coral #D95664; task, brand or approved reference colors take precedence. Blue and coral are the two inks; paper is not an ink. Overprints may create tones but no third independent ink. Gradients are disabled. Blue on paper is suggested for body text; coral on paper is decorative only at 3.24:1 contrast. Recheck actual compositing and text size.
motionAndInteraction: Reveal separated ink plates and swap printed forms; animate layers with masks or simple transforms. Keep grain fixed and offsets constant. For video, derive state from seekable composition time; for interactive HTML, finite scroll progress can coordinate chapters or story states, with coherent backward and direct seeking, readable holds, and reduced-motion/static behavior. Hover may isolate an illustration plate in the suggested hybrid. Avoid generic spring motion on every glyph.
audio: Unspecified as a fixed style rule. Choose music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience or silence for the subject and audience, honoring supplied audio requirements. Suggest a coherent direction and scene-level changes; keep speech clear, avoid clipping, and synchronize sound and picture.
assetRequirements: Create limited ink separations, controlled grain and stable registration offsets; composite layers and animate their reveals. SVG is a recommended style renderer for scalable shapes, masks and clipping paths. Python and Pillow can preprocess, composite and texture assets. Use authorized fonts, artwork and audio; load assets locally, seed randomness and cache stateful work. Distinguish simulated print appearance from physical production.
combinations: Can stand alone where two-ink overprint is the identity. With kinetic typography, reveal words as plates and reserve coral for large display text. With flat-vector illustration, map every fill to ink, overprint or paper, retaining figure proportions and grain only on fills. Supporting styles must collapse into two inks. Scroll-driven chapter transitions and story orchestration are optional when semantically useful; select one compatible transition and synchronized copy.
productionApproach: Choose the style renderer and motion engine for fidelity and action, with one owner per animated property. HyperFrames is the primary video composition and export pipeline; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, and record why. Pipelines handle timing, media/audio sync, validation and export, not visual construction. Integrate deterministic time-driven layers; inspect representative frames and the decoded video. For HTML, support scroll, keyboard, touch and reduced motion as applicable. Specific duration, format and deliverables are unspecified.
